description: Unify the cam loop around a single per-project tmux session: lazy-created host with orchestrator + dashboard panes, with plan/next/issue as thin pane launchers, an interactive menu that injects into the orchestrator, and orchestrator exit that tears the session down.

userStories.title: Project session module (tmux helpers)
userStories.description: As the cam codebase, I need a single tmux helper module so that all loop commands share one canonical way to name, create, and split into the per-project session.
acceptanceCriteria: New module under src/tmux/ (e.g. src/tmux/session.ts) exports projectSessionName, ensureProjectSession (lazy-creates the full session: orchestrator pane + dashboard pane, detached), openPaneInSession(session, cmd) (split-window -t against the project session), and isInsideProjectSession(env).
Helpers are pure with an injectable spawn (callers pass a spawn function; no direct global side-effects in unit tests).
Unit tests assert the exact tmux argv for new-session, split-window, and has-session (spawn-injected fake records calls).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-7 (single project session as host of all loop commands). Decided architecture (applies to whole cycle): one tmux session per project, name already exists as projectSessionName() in src/commands/run.ts = cam-orch-<base>-<hash>; loop commands open panes into it via split-window -t; lazy-create on first command with full layout (orchestrator pane + dashboard pane). Pattern: spawn-injected helpers tested by argv assertions (see existing tmux-related tests). Files: new src/tmux/session.ts; may extract projectSessionName from src/commands/run.ts and re-export. No external deps. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/regex access.

userStories.title: cam run uses the session module; dashboard becomes a permanent pane
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want cam run to assemble the project session via the shared module and run cam dashboard as the right-side pane so that the dashboard is captured from the very first command instead of being a separate UX surface.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/run.ts uses ensureProjectSession from the US-001 module to build the session (no duplicated session-creation logic).
Right pane runs `cam dashboard` (the binary keeps working, running inside the pane) instead of the static menu (interactive menu lands in US-004).
Unit tests assert the tmux argv produced by cam run (new-session + split-window for dashboard pane).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-8 (dashboard as permanent pane) and continues CAM-7. Depends on US-001. Files: src/commands/run.ts. Architecture reminder: one tmux session per project hosts everything; this story wires run.ts onto the shared module and promotes dashboard to a pane. Keep success/failure signalling on glyph, not divider color (Ink convention from lessons.md 2026-06-05) if any UI tweak slips in.

userStories.title: Orchestrator exit tears down the session
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want exiting the orchestrator (claude exit in pane 0) to kill the whole tmux session and drop me back into the shell so that I never have to ctrl+b d to leave.
acceptanceCriteria: Pane 0 command chains a `tmux kill-session -t <session>` after the claude invocation (or wires a pane-died/pane-exited hook) so that orchestrator exit terminates the session.
Unit test asserts the composed argv/script for pane 0 contains the kill-session call (or the hook registration argv).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-14 (exit drops back to terminal). Depends on US-002. Small story; touches src/commands/run.ts only. Mechanism: chain `; tmux kill-session -t <session>` to pane 0 command, or set-hook pane-died. Keep spawn-injected test style.

userStories.title: Interactive selectable menu that injects into the orchestrator
userStories.description: As a cam user inside the project session, I want the right-side menu pane to be an interactive selectable menu that sends the chosen command into the orchestrator pane so that I don't have to type commands manually.
acceptanceCriteria: buildRunMenuScript in src/commands/run.ts becomes a selectable key-loop menu (bash-style, same pattern as setup.ts which already uses `read -rsn1`).
On selection the menu invokes `tmux send-keys -t <orch-pane> <command> Enter` against the known orchestrator pane target (human-triggered action, not worker puppeteering).
Unit test asserts the generated menu script contains the expected send-keys argv / target pane reference for at least one menu entry.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-13 (menu pane becomes interactive). Depends on US-002 (dashboard already promoted; menu may sit alongside or replace, follow current run.ts layout decision). Pattern reference: setup.ts key-loop with `read -rsn1`. Files: src/commands/run.ts. Architecture reminder: orchestrator interacts with workers only via structured output + pane focus; this menu is human-triggered injection into a known pane, which is allowed.

userStories.title: Three-pane layout: orchestrator + permanent dashboard + interactive menu
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want the project session to host three panes (orchestrator, a permanent cam dashboard, and the interactive menu) so that the dashboard stays visible (US-002, US-010) while the menu also keeps its own pane (US-004), instead of the menu replacing the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: ensureProjectSession in src/tmux/session.ts builds a detached 3-pane layout (orchestrator pane + dashboard pane + menu pane). Unit tests assert the exact tmux argv (new-session plus the two split-window calls, with their target panes and the resulting pane ids).

src/commands/run.ts wires the dashboard pane to `cam dashboard` (permanent) and the menu pane to the interactive menu script. The dashboard is no longer replaced by the menu. The orchestrator pane target used by the menu send-keys and by the kill-session chain matches the actual orchestrator pane id after the 3-pane splits.
The stale header comment in run.ts (currently says pane 1 is `cam dashboard (permanent pane, US-002)`) is corrected to describe the real 3-pane layout.

The menu `d` entry is fixed: since the dashboard is now a permanent pane, either remove the `d` entry or repoint it to `tmux select-pane` the dashboard pane. It must NOT send the literal text `cam dashboard` into the claude orchestrator pane.
Existing US-001/US-002/US-004 tests are updated to the new pane targets and still pass.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Corrects the layout fork the PRD left unresolved: with only 2 panes the US-004 menu replaced the US-002 dashboard, contradicting US-002 (dashboard = permanent pane) and US-010 (operator smoke expects orchestrator + dashboard as panes). Operator chose the 3-pane layout (orchestrator + dashboard + menu) on 2026-06-05. Touches src/tmux/session.ts (3-pane build), src/commands/run.ts (dashboard + menu wiring, stale comment, d entry), and the affected tests. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/regex access. Keep the spawn-injected argv-assertion test style. The menu sends slash commands to the orchestrator pane 0.0; d should focus the dashboard pane, never inject text.

userStories.title: cam next becomes a pane launcher; stop is rewired
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want cam next to open the loop's claude as a pane in the project session (instead of creating a separate tmux session named 'cam') and cam stop to target the project session's pane so that everything lives in one session.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/next.ts opens the loop claude as a pane in the project session using the US-001 module (removes the standalone 'cam' session from buildTmuxSplitArgv).
src/commands/stop.ts targets the pane/session of the project (not the legacy 'cam' session).
Unit tests assert the new tmux argv for both commands (spawn-injected; no real tmux).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-9 (plan/next as pane launchers, ripples on stop). Depends on US-001. Files: src/commands/next.ts, src/commands/stop.ts. Architecture reminder: thin launcher pattern - command ensures session, opens pane, returns to shell; interaction migrates inside the session. Today buildTmuxSplitArgv in next.ts creates the 'cam' session - that path is removed by this story.

userStories.title: cam plan becomes a pane launcher
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want cam plan to open /cam-plan as a pane in the project session (no more foreground PTY) so that APPROVE is answered inside the pane and the plan run shows up alongside the orchestrator and dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/plan.ts opens the /cam-plan claude invocation as a pane in the project session via the US-001 module; the PTY/foreground inherit path is removed.
APPROVE interaction happens inside the pane (the elegant approve-via-flag is CAM-12, explicitly out of scope here).
Unit test asserts the new tmux argv for cam plan.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-9 (plan as pane launcher). Depends on US-001. Files: src/commands/plan.ts. Architecture reminder: end of PTY/inherit foreground in cam plan; pane in the project session is the host. APPROVE inside pane for this cycle; flag-file approve is post-MVP (CAM-12).

userStories.title: New subcommand cam issue <free text>
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want to run `cam issue "<free text>"` from any terminal to file an issue without entering a session manually, so that issue creation is a first-class CLI verb instead of being reachable only via the /cam-issue slash inside a session.
acceptanceCriteria: index.ts dispatches a new `issue` subcommand to a new src/commands/issue.ts.

issue.ts reads permission_mode from project config, ensures the project session via the US-001 module, and opens a pane with claude receiving the free-text argument (which expands to title + description and runs /cam-issue create).
A help block for `cam issue` is registered in src/logging/help.ts.
No --permission-mode CLI flag is registered (invariant; test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts must keep passing).
Unit tests assert: dispatch wiring in index.ts, the tmux argv used to open the pane, and that the help block exists.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-11 (cam issue free-text subcommand). Depends on US-001. Files: index.ts (dispatch), src/commands/issue.ts (new), src/logging/help.ts (help block). Architecture reminder: command doesn't steal the TTY - opens a pane in the project session; output is visible by attaching via cam run. Hard invariant: never register --permission-mode flag (enforced by test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts; see scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md Codebase Patterns).

userStories.title: Post-exec hint suggesting cam run when detached
userStories.description: As a cam user, I want loop commands that finish outside the project tmux session to print a short hint telling me to attach via `cam run`, and to suppress the hint when I'm already inside the session, so that I never lose track of where the panes are.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared helper (e.g. in src/logging/screen.ts or a small util) emits a short attach hint referencing `cam run` only when isInsideProjectSession(env) is false.
cam plan, cam next, and cam issue call the helper at the end of their successful path.
Unit tests assert: hint printed when env signals detached; hint suppressed when env signals inside session.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Funds CAM-10 (post-exec attach hint). Depends on US-005, US-006, US-007 (call sites). Files: src/logging/screen.ts (or new util) and call sites src/commands/plan.ts, src/commands/next.ts, src/commands/issue.ts. Detection uses isInsideProjectSession from US-001 (likely TMUX env var matching the project session name).

userStories.title: Docs reflect the new single-session model
userStories.description: As a cam user reading docs, I want HELP blocks, README, and FLOW.md to describe the single project session, pane launchers, dashboard-as-pane, cam issue, and orchestrator-exit teardown so that documentation matches behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: RUN_HELP, NEXT_HELP, PLAN_HELP, DASHBOARD_HELP in index.ts describe the new model (single session, launchers, dashboard as pane, exit teardown).
README.md updated for the new flow and the cam issue subcommand.
FLOW.md updated to reflect the new flow.
No em-dash (—) characters in any persisted .md (project preference).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Doc maintenance for the new model. Depends on US-001 through US-008. Files: index.ts (HELP strings), README.md, FLOW.md. Project preference: no em-dash in persisted .md (substitute colon, comma, parens, period, or rephrase). Do not announce absence (omit cross-refs that only say content lives elsewhere).

userStories.title: Operator smoke in a real terminal
userStories.description: As the operator, I need to validate end-to-end in a real terminal that the session, panes, menu, and exit teardown actually behave as specified so that the cycle ships with confidence.
acceptanceCriteria: `cam run` brings up the session with orchestrator + dashboard as panes (operator confirms visually).
`cam next`, `cam plan`, and `cam issue "..."` open panes in the same session when run from another terminal.
The interactive menu navigates with keys and injects the selected command into the orchestrator pane.
Typing `exit` in the orchestrator pane kills the tmux session and returns the operator to the shell (no ctrl+b d needed).
Operator flips passes:true after confirming each of the above.
userStories.notes: Operator ceremony: not autonomous. The user already volunteered to run `cam run` in a real terminal. Depends on US-001 through US-009. The cam-loop falls through this story automatically; only the operator can mark it passed.
